verbalization: Doxorubicin is associated with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) through a series of indications that link it to AML with a specific translocation, T(8;16)(p11;p13). The evidence suggests that Doxorubicin is used to treat AML with the T(9;11)(p22;q23) translocation, which is a known subset of AML. This translocation is also linked to Aldesleukin, which in turn is indicated for the same AML subtype. The presence of this translocation in the target condition implies a shared pathophysiological mechanism, possibly involving the activation of certain signaling pathways or the expression of specific genes. The integration of these indications suggests that Doxorubicin may exert its therapeutic effect through a mechanism that is relevant to the molecular profile of AML with this translocation. The evidence supports a potential role for Doxorubicin in the treatment of this AML subtype, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
